stem.en:
A bell maker pours melted bronze into a clay mold and then leaves the new bell buried in sand for several days. If the metal cools too ______, she explains, the bell may crack or ring out of tune.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

why.en: Burying the bell in sand for days makes it cool slowly; the warning is against the opposite, cooling too quickly. Cooling "gently" or "evenly" is no danger, and "loudly" does not describe cooling.
why.uz: Qoʻngʻiroqni bir necha kun qumga koʻmish uni sekin sovitadi; ogohlantirish buning aksi — juda tez sovishdan. «Gently» yoki «evenly» sovish xavfli emas, «loudly» esa sovishni tasvirlamaydi.
why.ru: Колокол днями лежит в песке, чтобы остывать медленно; опасно обратное — остыть слишком быстро. Остывать «gently» или «evenly» не опасно, а «loudly» к остыванию не подходит.

In the story, the old mapmaker Rustam is known throughout his town for his ______. When a visitor praises a map that took him a whole year to draw, he only nods, rolls the map up, and goes back to his desk without a word.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

why.en: Rustam meets praise with a nod and no words: he is known for saying little. Eloquence is skill with words, candor is frankness, and extravagance is excess; the scene shows none of them.
why.uz: Rustam maqtovga soʻzsiz bosh irgʻab javob beradi: u kamgapligi bilan tanilgan. «Eloquence» — notiqlik, «candor» — ochiqlik, «extravagance» — isrofgarchilik; sahnada ulardan hech biri yoʻq.

stem.en:
Every spring, one mountain village holds an unusual race in which teams carry a full jug of water up a steep hill. The winner is not the fastest team but the team whose jug is fullest at the top. As a result, the best teams climb at a steady, careful pace, while teams that rush usually reach the top with half-empty jugs.

Which choice best describes the function of the second sentence in the text as a whole?

options.en: It gives the rule that explains how the teams behave in the rest of the text.
It argues that the race would be fairer if the fastest team were named the winner.
It describes the steep hill that every team must climb.
It names the village where the race is held each spring.

why.en: The second sentence gives the rule, the fullest jug wins, and the third follows from it ("As a result"). It makes no argument, does not describe the hill, and names no village.
why.uz: Ikkinchi gap qoidani beradi — koʻzasi eng toʻla jamoa yutadi, uchinchi gap shundan kelib chiqadi («As a result»). U daʼvo qilmaydi, tepalikni tasvirlamaydi, qishloq nomini aytmaydi.
why.ru: Второе предложение даёт правило — побеждает самый полный кувшин, а третье из него вытекает («As a result»). Оно ничего не доказывает, не описывает холм и не называет деревню.

stem.en:
Many people imagine that a weather forecaster simply reads tomorrow's weather from a computer screen. In fact, the computer produces several possible forecasts, and they often disagree. The forecaster's real work is to judge which of them best fits what she knows about the local hills, winds, and lakes, and then to explain her choice in plain words.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It presents a common belief about a job and then describes what the job actually involves.
It describes a method of forecasting, lists its faults, and then recommends a newer method instead.
It compares two forecasters who disagree about how far computers can be trusted.
It explains how computers produce forecasts and why their forecasts never disagree.

why.en: The first sentence gives a common belief; "In fact" turns to the real work: choosing among disagreeing forecasts and explaining the choice. No method is rejected and no two forecasters appear.
why.uz: Birinchi gapda keng tarqalgan fikr beriladi; «In fact» dan keyin asl ish keladi: bir-biriga zid prognozlardan birini tanlash va tushuntirish. Usul rad etilmaydi, ikki sinoptik yoʻq.
why.ru: Первое предложение даёт распространённое мнение; после «In fact» — настоящая работа: выбрать из расходящихся прогнозов и объяснить выбор. Метод не отвергается, двух синоптиков нет.

stem.en:
Text 1
In several river valleys, people want to bring back beavers, which once lived there. Supporters point to the ponds that beavers build with their dams: the ponds slow floods, store water for the dry months, and give fish and birds new places to live.

Text 2
The benefits of beaver ponds are real, but they are not free. Where farms now line a river, the same ponds can flood fields and block the ditches that drain them. Bringing beavers back works best in valleys with room for the water to spread, or where farmers are paid for the land the ponds take.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the supporters described in Text 1?

options.en: By agreeing that beaver ponds have benefits while warning that they can harm farms in some valleys
By arguing that beaver ponds make floods worse instead of slowing them, as the supporters claim
By denying that beavers ever lived in the river valleys where people now want to bring them back
By insisting that farmers be paid for every beaver pond in every valley before any beavers are allowed to return

why.en: Text 2 calls the benefits "real" but warns that ponds can flood fields where farms line a river, so the plan suits some valleys only. It denies nothing, and payment is one option, not a demand.
why.uz: 2-matn foydalarni «real» deydi, lekin fermalar bor joyda hovuzlar dalani suv bostirishi mumkinligini aytadi: reja faqat baʼzi vodiylarga mos. U hech narsani inkor etmaydi, toʻlov esa talab emas.
why.ru: Text 2 называет пользу «real», но предупреждает: где вдоль реки фермы, пруды топят поля, так что план годится не везде. Он ничего не отрицает, а оплата — один из вариантов, а не требование.

stem.en:
Nodira had never repaired anything more complicated than a bicycle chain, but when her grandmother's old sewing machine jammed, she decided to try. She borrowed a repair guide from the library, laid out every screw on a clean cloth in the order she removed it, and spent three evenings cleaning and testing each part. On the fourth evening, the needle moved smoothly again.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: Through patient, careful work, Nodira succeeds at a repair that is new to her.
Nodira's grandmother teaches her how to repair an old sewing machine.
Nodira finds that the library has no guide that can help her with the repair.
Nodira gives up on the sewing machine and goes back to repairing bicycles.

why.en: Nodira, new to such repairs, works slowly and carefully for three evenings, and on the fourth the machine works. She uses a library guide, not her grandmother's lessons, and she does not give up.
why.uz: Bunday taʼmirni birinchi qilayotgan Nodira uch oqshom sabr bilan ishlaydi, toʻrtinchisida mashina ishlaydi. U buvisidan emas, kutubxona qoʻllanmasidan oʻrganadi va taslim boʻlmaydi.
why.ru: Нодира, впервые взявшаяся за такой ремонт, три вечера работает терпеливо и аккуратно, и на четвёртый машинка снова шьёт. Она пользуется руководством из библиотеки, а не уроками бабушки, и не сдаётся.

stem.en:
Visitors to Zarina's calligraphy class are often surprised that she has beginners write with a reed pen for their whole first month, although a steel nib would give them neater letters from the first day. The reed, she explains, punishes every careless angle with a blot, so students learn to feel the right angle in their fingers. Once they have that feeling, she says, any better pen makes them better at once.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: Zarina starts beginners on a reed pen because it shows each wrong angle at once, which trains a feel for the pen that a neater nib would hide.
Zarina starts beginners on a reed pen because its slow, scratchy strokes teach them a patience that a faster pen would never ask of them.
Zarina starts beginners on a reed pen because learning on the tool of the old masters gives them a respect for the craft that a modern pen would not.
Zarina starts beginners on a reed pen because a month with a poor pen makes them grateful for the better pens that come after it.

why.en: Each careless angle leaves a blot, so beginners learn to feel the right angle, which a neater steel nib would hide. Patience, the old masters and gratitude are never mentioned.

stem.en:
An aquarium recorded its visitors over one weekend.

Day | Morning | Afternoon
Saturday | 340 | 520
Sunday | 410 | 290

The aquarium's manager noticed that on Saturday more people visited in the afternoon than in the morning, but on Sunday ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

options.en: the morning was busier, with 410 visitors against 290.
the afternoon was busier, with 410 against 290.
the afternoon had 520 visitors, the most of any half-day.
the morning had 340 visitors, fewer than the afternoon.

why.en: On Sunday the morning had 410 visitors and the afternoon 290, the reverse of Saturday's pattern. 520 and 340 are Saturday's figures, and on Sunday the afternoon was not the busier half.
why.uz: Yakshanba kuni ertalab 410, tushdan keyin 290 kishi kelgan — shanbaning teskarisi. 520 va 340 shanbaga tegishli, yakshanba kuni esa tushdan keyingi vaqt gavjumroq boʻlmagan.
why.ru: В воскресенье утром пришло 410 человек, а днём 290 — наоборот по сравнению с субботой. 520 и 340 — субботние числа, а в воскресенье вторая половина дня не была многолюднее.

stem.en:
A student measured how much electricity the small solar panel on her family's roof produced on four days in May. A bar graph shows the results in watt-hours: Monday (sunny) 410, Tuesday (cloudy) 160, Wednesday (sunny) 395 and Thursday (partly cloudy) 270.

The student concluded that cloud cover sharply reduces how much electricity the panel produces.

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support the student's conclusion?

options.en: On cloudy Tuesday the panel produced 160 watt-hours, less than half of the 410 it produced on sunny Monday.
On sunny Wednesday the panel produced 395 watt-hours, almost as much as the 410 it produced on Monday.
On partly cloudy Thursday the panel produced 270 watt-hours, more than it produced on sunny Wednesday.
On cloudy Tuesday the panel produced 160 watt-hours, more than it produced on any of the other three days.

why.en: A cloudy day set against a sunny one shows the clouds' effect: 160 against 410, less than half. Two sunny days say nothing of clouds, 270 is less than 395, and 160 is the lowest value.
why.uz: Bulutli kunni quyoshli kun bilan solishtirish bulut taʼsirini koʻrsatadi: 160 ga qarshi 410, yarmidan kam. Ikki quyoshli kun bulutni koʻrsatmaydi, 270 esa 395 dan kam, 160 — eng past qiymat.
why.ru: Облачный день против солнечного показывает влияние облаков: 160 против 410, меньше половины. Два солнечных дня об облаках молчат, 270 меньше 395, а 160 — наименьшее значение.

stem.en:
Students noticed that great tits nesting in boxes in a city park seemed to raise more chicks in the boxes on the quiet east side of the park than in those on the west side, which runs along a busy road. They hypothesized that traffic noise reduces the number of chicks the birds raise.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the students' hypothesis?

options.en: In another park, where the busy road runs along the east side, the birds raised more chicks in the boxes on the quiet west side.
In a year when the road was closed for repairs, the birds in the west-side boxes still raised fewer chicks than those in the east.
The birds in the west-side boxes started building their nests a few days earlier each spring than those on the east side.
Most of the chicks raised on both sides of the park left their boxes during the first weeks of summer.

why.en: If the gap moves with the road to whichever side it runs along, noise, not the side of the park, explains it. Fewer chicks in the west even with the road closed would point away from noise.
why.uz: Agar farq yoʻl bilan birga u qaysi tomonda boʻlsa, oʻsha tomonga koʻchsa, sabab bogʻning tomoni emas, shovqin. Yoʻl yopiq paytda ham gʻarbda jojalar kam boʻlsa, sabab shovqin boʻlmasdi.
why.ru: Если разница переходит вместе с дорогой на ту сторону, где она идёт, дело в шуме, а не в стороне парка. Меньше птенцов на западе при закрытой дороге говорило бы против шума.

stem.en:
For a month, the main exit of the city's train station was closed for repairs, and passengers had to leave by a side exit on the far side of the building. Kiosks near the side exit had their busiest month of the year, while kiosks by the main exit had their quietest. Since the main exit reopened, sales at both groups of kiosks have returned to their usual levels. This pattern suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: much of the kiosks' business depends on which way passengers leave the station.
the repairs made the main exit much less popular with passengers than it had been before.
passengers spent more money at the station during the month the main exit was closed.
kiosks near the side exit sell goods that passengers cannot find anywhere else nearby.

why.en: Sales rose where passengers now left, fell where they no longer passed, and returned to normal with the exit: business follows the route. No total spending is given.
why.uz: Savdo yoʻlovchilar endi chiqadigan joyda oshgan, ular oʻtmay qoʻygan joyda kamaygan, asosiy chiqish ochilgach odatiy holga qaytgan: savdo yoʻnalishga bogʻliq. Umumiy xarajat berilmagan.
why.ru: Продажи выросли там, где теперь выходили пассажиры, упали там, где они не проходили, и вернулись вместе с выходом: торговля зависит от пути. Общих трат в тексте нет.

stem.en:

the fish eat the algae that make the water green and cloudy.
water fleas make the lake green and cloudy in years when they are common.
clear water makes it harder for the fish to find water fleas.

stem.en:
Most birds build their nests and raise their young in spring. ______ crossbills, which feed on the seeds inside pine cones, sometimes nest in the middle of winter, when the cones are full of seeds.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

why.en: Nesting in winter differs from the usual spring nesting, so a contrast is needed: "However". Crossbills are an exception, not an example, a result or a similar case.
why.uz: Qishda uya qurish odatdagi bahorgi uya qurishdan farq qiladi, shuning uchun qarama-qarshilik kerak: «However». Bu qushlar istisno: misol, natija yoki oʻxshash holat emas.
why.ru: Гнездование зимой отличается от обычного весеннего, поэтому нужно противопоставление: «However». Клесты — исключение, а не пример, следствие или сходный случай.

stem.en:
The museum had planned to build a new wing for its growing collection of fossils. ______ it turned two unused storerooms into galleries and spent the money it saved on cleaning and repairing its oldest fossils.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

why.en: The museum planned a new wing but used its storerooms: it did something in place of its plan, so "Instead" fits. Using the storerooms is not an example, a result or a similar action.
why.uz: Muzey yangi qanot qurmoqchi edi, lekin omborlarni ishlatdi: rejasi oʻrniga boshqa ish qildi, shuning uchun «Instead» mos. Bu misol, natija yoki oʻxshash harakat emas.
why.ru: Музей собирался строить новое крыло, но занял кладовые: сделал другое вместо задуманного, поэтому подходит «Instead». Это не пример, не следствие и не похожее действие.

stem.en:
Many people believe that bats are blind. ______ most bats can see quite well, and many of them also find their way in the dark by listening to the echoes of their own calls.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

why.en: The second sentence corrects the belief in the first, so "In reality" fits. It does not follow from the belief, it does not add to it, and it does not restate the belief in other words.
why.uz: Ikkinchi gap birinchi gapdagi qarashni tuzatadi, shuning uchun «In reality» mos. U bu qarashdan kelib chiqmaydi, unga qoʻshimcha emas va uni boshqa soʻzlar bilan takrorlamaydi.
why.ru: Второе предложение исправляет мнение из первого, поэтому подходит «In reality». Оно не вытекает из этого мнения, не дополняет его и не пересказывает другими словами.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The Quince Fair is held each October in a small hill town.
• Growers bring more than fifteen kinds of quince.
• Visitors can taste quince jam for free.
• A prize goes to the largest quince of the year.

The student wants to tell readers when and where the fair takes place.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: The Quince Fair takes place each October in a small hill town.
At the Quince Fair, growers bring more than fifteen kinds of quince.
Visitors to the Quince Fair can taste the growers' quince jam for free.
At the fair, a prize goes to the grower of the largest quince of the year.

why.en: Only this choice gives both the time, each October, and the place, a small hill town. The others describe what happens at the fair.
why.uz: Faqat shu javob ham vaqtni — har oktyabr, ham joyni — tepalikdagi kichik shaharchani beradi. Qolganlari yarmarkada nima boʻlishini tasvirlaydi.
why.ru: Только этот вариант называет и время — каждый октябрь, и место — городок на холмах. Остальные описывают, что происходит на ярмарке.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Two hot springs lie in the same mountain valley.
• The water of the North Spring is 38°C; that of the South Spring is 52°C.
• The North Spring is next to the road; the South Spring is a two-hour walk away.
• Both springs stay warm through the winter.
• At both springs, the water smells faintly of sulfur.

The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two springs.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Both springs stay warm through the winter, and at each the water smells faintly of sulfur.
The water of the South Spring, at 52°C, is far hotter than the 38°C water of the North Spring.
The North Spring is next to the road, while the South Spring is a two-hour walk away.
The South Spring, a two-hour walk from the road, has water as hot as 52°C.

why.en: A similarity is something both springs share: they stay warm all winter and smell faintly of sulfur. The other choices give differences in heat and distance, or describe one spring only.
why.uz: Oʻxshashlik — ikkala buloqda ham bor narsa: qishda ham iliq qoladi va suvidan oltingugurt hidi keladi. Qolganlari harorat va masofadagi farqni beradi yoki faqat bitta buloqni tasvirlaydi.
why.ru: Сходство — то, что есть у обоих источников: они тёплые всю зиму, и вода слегка пахнет серой. Остальные варианты называют различия в температуре и расстоянии или описывают один источник.

stem.en:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• A scout troop tested three kinds of tinder for lighting a fire in damp weather.
• Grass caught fire after an average of 40 seconds.
• Pine needles caught fire after an average of 25 seconds.
• Birch bark caught fire after an average of 8 seconds.
• The troop concluded that birch bark is the best tinder to carry on wet days.

The student wants to present the troop's conclusion and the evidence for it.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.en: Birch bark caught fire in 8 seconds on average, far sooner than pine needles or grass, so the troop judged it the best tinder for wet days.
The troop tested three kinds of tinder, grass, pine needles and birch bark, to see which lights fastest in damp weather.
The troop concluded that birch bark is the best kind of tinder for scouts to carry with them on wet days.
Grass took an average of 40 seconds to catch fire, while pine needles took an average of 25 seconds.

why.en: Only this choice gives both the conclusion, birch bark is best, and the evidence, 8 seconds against 25 and 40. The others give only the method, only the conclusion, or only the slower results.
why.uz: Faqat shu javob ham xulosani — qayin poʻstlogʻi eng yaxshisi, ham dalilni — 25 va 40 ga qarshi 8 soniyani beradi. Qolganlari faqat usulni, faqat xulosani yoki faqat sekinroq natijalarni beradi.
why.ru: Только этот вариант даёт и вывод — берёста лучше всего, и доказательство — 8 секунд против 25 и 40. Остальные дают лишь метод, лишь вывод или лишь более медленные результаты.

stem.en:
The engineers' report on the town's new water system was ______: it described every pump, pipe, and storage tank in such detail that another team could have rebuilt the whole system from the report alone.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

why.en: A report detailed enough to rebuild the whole system from covers everything: it is exhaustive. Nothing suggests it took sides, and "hasty" and "vague" contradict its detail.
why.uz: Butun tizimni qayta qurishga yetadigan batafsil hisobot hamma narsani qamraydi: u mukammal. Uning kimningdir tarafini olgani aytilmagan, «hasty» va «vague» esa batafsillikka zid.
why.ru: Отчёт, по которому можно заново построить всю систему, охватывает всё: он исчерпывающий. О пристрастности («biased») ничего не сказано, а «hasty» и «vague» противоречат описанной подробности.

stem.en:
Although the two dialects share most of their words, speakers of one often find the other ______ at first, since the same words are pronounced so differently that even a familiar phrase can sound entirely new.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

why.en: Familiar phrases that "sound entirely new" confuse a listener at first, so "baffling" fits. "Identical" contradicts the different sounds, and nothing calls the dialect dull or rude.
why.uz: «Butunlay yangi» eshitiladigan tanish iboralar avvaliga tinglovchini dovdiratadi: «baffling». «Identical» turli talaffuzga zid, sheva zerikarli yoki qoʻpol ekani esa aytilmagan.
why.ru: Знакомые фразы, которые «звучат совсем по-новому», поначалу сбивают с толку: «baffling». «Identical» противоречит разному произношению, а скучным или грубым диалект не назван.

stem.en:
The composer's early pieces were admired for their rich harmonies but faulted for melodies that seemed ______; listeners complained that the tunes never surprised them, moving through the expected notes in the expected order.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

why.en: Tunes that never surprise and move through "the expected notes in the expected order" follow a set pattern: formulaic. "Erratic" is the opposite, and "haunting" is praise.
why.uz: Hech qachon hayratlantirmaydigan, «kutilgan notalarni kutilgan tartibda» chaladigan kuylar qolipga tushgan: «formulaic». «Erratic» buning aksi, «haunting» esa maqtov.
why.ru: Мелодии, которые никогда не удивляют и идут «ожидаемыми нотами в ожидаемом порядке», шаблонны: «formulaic». «Erratic» — противоположность, «haunting» — похвала, а о незаконченности мелодий не сказано.

stem.en:
Far from being a ______ addition to the old village, the new school was designed around it: its walls are built of the same pale stone as the houses, its roof follows the slope of the hill, and its gate opens onto the village square.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

why.en: "Far from being" introduces the opposite of what follows: the school was built to fit the village, so it was far from jarring. "Harmonious" and "suitable" describe what it is.
why.uz: «Far from being» keyingi fikrga zid narsani kiritadi: maktab qishloqqa moslab qurilgan, demak u «jarring» emas. «Harmonious» va «suitable» uning aslida qandayligini bildiradi.
why.ru: «Far from being» вводит противоположность тому, что дальше: школу вписали в деревню, значит, она не «jarring». «Harmonious» и «suitable» описывают, какова она на самом деле.

stem.en:
For years, the fishermen on one lake blamed cormorants, birds that dive for fish, for their shrinking catch. To test the idea, a group of fishermen kept the birds away from one bay for a whole season using nets and noise. The catch in that bay fell just as much as in the rest of the lake, so the fishermen began looking for another cause, and they eventually traced the problem to the water's rising temperature.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It presents an explanation, describes a test of it, and reports that the test pointed to another cause.
It describes a problem, proposes two possible solutions to it, and then argues that neither of them would work.
It explains how cormorants catch fish and then describes how the fishermen catch them.
It compares two groups of fishermen who disagree about why their catch has been shrinking.

why.en: The text gives an explanation (the birds), a test of it (keeping them away) and a result that led to a new cause (warmer water). No solutions are weighed and no two groups disagree.
why.uz: Matn tushuntirishni (qushlar), uning sinovini (qushlarni haydash) va yangi sababga (iliqroq suv) olib kelgan natijani beradi. Yechimlar tortishilmaydi, bahslashgan guruhlar yoʻq.
why.ru: Текст даёт объяснение рыбаков (птицы), проверку (птиц отгоняли) и результат, который привёл к новой причине (тёплая вода). Решения не взвешиваются, способы ловли не сравниваются, спорящих групп нет.

stem.en:
The following text is from a story. Dilbar has come home after five years abroad.

The street had not changed, or so it seemed at first. The same plane trees leaned over the same blue gate, and the same smell of fresh bread drifted from the bakery on the corner. Only when she reached the gate did Dilbar notice that the bench beside it, where her father had sat every evening, was gone.

Which choice best describes the function of the final sentence in the text as a whole?

options.en: It reveals a change that undercuts the sense of sameness built up in the earlier sentences.
It explains why Dilbar has decided to come home after five years abroad.
It introduces a new character who is waiting for Dilbar at the gate.
It adds one more detail to the list of familiar things on the street that have stayed exactly the same.

why.en: The earlier sentences stress sameness ("the same" three times); the last reveals a loss, her father's bench, foreshadowed by "or so it seemed at first". It shows change, not sameness.
why.uz: Oldingi gaplar oʻzgarmaganlikni taʼkidlaydi (uch marta «the same»); oxirgisi yoʻqotishni — otasining oʻrindigʻini ochadi, buni «or so it seemed at first» sezdiradi.
why.ru: Предыдущие предложения подчёркивают неизменность (трижды «the same»); последнее открывает потерю — скамейку отца, что предвещает «or so it seemed at first». Это перемена, а не сходство.

stem.en:
Text 1
Historians long assumed that the small stone fort above the mountain pass was built to guard a trade route. But a recent dig there found no coins, seals, or merchants' goods, only weapons and grain jars. The fort, the diggers concluded, must have served a purely military purpose.

Text 2
An absence of merchants' goods at a fort does not show that traders never passed it. Guards at such a post would have inspected goods, not kept them, and any coins taken as tolls would have been sent on to the city's treasury. A fort that guarded a trade route might leave behind little more than what its soldiers needed: weapons and food.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the diggers' conclusion in Text 1?

options.en: By arguing that the dig's finds are just what a fort guarding a trade route might leave behind
By agreeing that the weapons and grain jars show that the fort had nothing to do with trade
By suggesting that more digging will uncover the coins and seals still buried at the fort
By questioning whether the weapons and grain jars really date from the time the fort was built

why.en: Text 2 explains why a fort on a trade route would keep no goods or coins and leave only weapons and food, just what was found. It rejects the conclusion and predicts no new finds.
why.uz: 2-matn savdo yoʻlidagi qalʼada nega mol va tanga qolmasligini, faqat qurol va oziq qolishini tushuntiradi — aynan topilganlar. U xulosani rad etadi, yangi topilma kutmaydi.
why.ru: Text 2 объясняет, почему крепость на торговом пути не хранила товаров и монет и оставила лишь оружие и еду — то, что нашли. Он отвергает вывод и не ждёт новых находок.

instructions.en: Read both texts. Decide how the ideas in them relate to each other.
instructions.uz: Ikkala matnni oʻqing. Ulardagi gʻoyalar bir-biri bilan qanday bogʻlanishini aniqlang.
instructions.ru: Прочитайте оба текста. Определите, как связаны их идеи.

stem.en:
Each spring, the households along one village's irrigation canal clean it together before the water is let in. The work is shared by length: every household clears the stretch of canal in front of its own land, and households with no land along the canal bring food for the workers.

According to the text, how is the cleaning of the canal shared out?

options.en: Each household clears the stretch of canal in front of its own land.
Only the households with no land along the canal do the cleaning.
The households hire workers and divide the cost among themselves.
Each household cleans the whole canal once every few years, in turn.

why.en: The text says "every household clears the stretch of canal in front of its own land". Households without land bring food rather than clean, no one is hired, and no one cleans the whole canal.
why.uz: Matnda «har bir xonadon oʻz yeri roʻparasidagi kanal qismini tozalaydi», deyilgan. Yeri yoʻq xonadonlar tozalamaydi, ovqat olib keladi, hech kim yollanmaydi, butun kanalni ham hech kim tozalamaydi.
why.ru: В тексте сказано, что каждый двор чистит участок канала напротив своей земли. Дворы без земли не чистят, а приносят еду, никого не нанимают, и весь канал никто не чистит.

stem.en:
When one city cut its bus fares in half, officials expected far more people to ride. Ridership rose, but by less than a tenth. Surveys found that most people who drove did so not because of the fare but because the buses came only twice an hour, while those who already rode the bus simply paid less. When the city later added enough buses for them to come every ten minutes, ridership rose by a third, even though fares had returned to their old level.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: For this city's potential riders, how often buses came mattered more than what a ride cost.
Cutting bus fares in half caused the number of bus riders in the city to double.
Most drivers in the city said in the surveys that they would never ride a bus, whatever the fare or schedule.
Running buses more often costs a city more than lowering its bus fares does.

why.en: Halving fares added under a tenth more riders; buses every ten minutes added a third at the old fares. So frequency mattered more than price. Ridership did not double, and no costs are compared.
why.uz: Narxni yarmiga tushirish yoʻlovchini oʻndan birdan kam koʻpaytirdi; har oʻn daqiqada avtobus esa eski narxda uchdan birga oshirdi. Demak qatnov narxdan muhimroq.
why.ru: Цена вдвое ниже дала меньше десятой части новых пассажиров, а автобус каждые десять минут при старой цене — треть. Значит, частота важнее цены; затраты не сравниваются.

stem.en:
Dilshod argues that the new signs warning drivers about deer on the mountain road have reduced the number of collisions between cars and deer there.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Dilshod's argument?

options.en: In the year after the signs went up, collisions with deer on the road were as frequent as in the year before.
The new signs are bright yellow and stand at both ends of the stretch of road where deer most often cross it.
Collisions with deer on other mountain roads in the region, which have no signs, did not change over the same year.
More drivers now use the mountain road in summer than in winter, when snow often closes it for days.

why.en: If collisions were as frequent after the signs as before, the signs did not reduce them. Unchanged collisions on roads without signs would support Dilshod, and the rest is beside the point.
why.uz: Agar belgilardan keyin toʻqnashuvlar avvalgidek koʻp boʻlsa, belgilar ularni kamaytirmagan. Belgisiz yoʻllardagi oʻzgarmagan holat Dilshodni quvvatlardi, qolganlari aloqasiz.
why.ru: Если после знаков столкновений столько же, сколько до, знаки их не сократили. Неизменность на дорогах без знаков поддержала бы Дилшода, а остальное к делу не относится.

instructions.en: Choose the finding that most weakens the claim in the text.
instructions.uz: Matndagi daʼvoni eng koʻp zaiflashtiradigan natijani tanlang.
instructions.ru: Выберите результат, который сильнее всего ослабляет утверждение в тексте.

stem.en:
Some ecologists have suggested that foxes living in cities are bolder around people than foxes in the countryside because city foxes grow used to people, not because they are born bolder. To test this, a team raised fox cubs born to city parents and cubs born to country parents in the same quiet enclosure, far from people.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the ecologists' suggestion?

options.en: As adults, the foxes born to city parents and those born to country parents approached a stranger with the same caution.
As adults, the foxes born to city parents approached a stranger far sooner than those born to country parents.
The cubs born to city parents grew larger than the cubs born to country parents.
Wild foxes in the city were seen near houses far more often than wild foxes in the countryside.

why.en: If foxes raised alike, far from people, are equally cautious whatever their parents, boldness is learned, not inborn. Bolder city-born foxes would point to birth instead.
why.uz: Odamlardan uzoqda bir xil oʻstirilgan tulkilar ota-onasidan qatʼi nazar bir xil ehtiyotkor boʻlsa, jasurlik tugʻma emas, orttirilgan. Shahar zotlari jasurroq boʻlsa, sabab tugʻilishda boʻlardi.

stem.en:
A student recorded the share of seeds that sprouted for three crops, each planted at three depths.

Crop | 1 cm deep | 3 cm deep | 5 cm deep
Lentil | 62% | 48% | 81%
Chickpea | 55% | 70% | 74%

The student claims that no single planting depth was the best for all three crops.

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the student's claim?

options.en: Lentils and chickpeas did best at 5 cm, but peas did best at 3 cm, 66% against 58% at 5 cm.
All three crops sprouted less often at 1 cm than at 5 cm, by at least 18 percentage points.
Lentils planted at 5 cm sprouted 81% of the time, the highest share recorded anywhere in the table.
Chickpeas sprouted best at 3 cm, at 70%, compared with only 55% at 1 cm.

why.en: The claim needs a crop with a different best depth: lentils and chickpeas peaked at 5 cm, peas at 3 cm. The other facts do not bear on it, and chickpeas did better at 5 cm (74%) than at 3 cm (70%).
why.uz: Daʼvo uchun eng yaxshi chuqurligi boshqacha ekin kerak: yasmiq va noʻxat 5 sm da, koʻk noʻxat 3 sm da eng yaxshi unib chiqqan. Noʻxat esa 5 sm da (74%) 3 sm dagidan (70%) yaxshiroq.
why.ru: Нужна культура с другой лучшей глубиной: чечевица и нут лучше всего взошли на 5 см, горох — на 3 см. Остальное к утверждению не относится, а нут на 5 см (74%) взошёл лучше, чем на 3 см (70%).

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: moved some buyers from online to the box office without reducing total sales.
led many people who once bought tickets online to stop going to concerts at the hall.
made the hall's concerts more popular than they had been before.
was too small for any of the hall's ticket buyers to notice or care about.

why.en: Online sales fell, box-office sales rose by about as many, and the total held: buyers switched where they bought. The steady total rules out lost or new audiences; the online drop shows they noticed.

Pollen preserved in the layers of mud at the bottom of a lake shows which plants grew nearby in each period. In the layers from about 2,000 years ago, pollen from wheat and barley suddenly appears, while pollen from oak trees becomes scarce. Since wheat and barley do not grow wild in the region, and since farmers of that era often cleared forests to make fields, these layers suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: people began farming near the lake at about that time, clearing much of the oak forest.
the climate around the lake turned too cold for oak trees to survive.
wheat and barley had grown wild around the lake for thousands of years before.
oak trees spread across the area as farmers abandoned their fields beside the lake.

why.en: Crops that do not grow wild appear as the oaks fade, and farmers then cleared forests for fields: people began farming and cut the oaks. No cold is mentioned, and the oaks did not spread.
why.uz: Yovvoyi oʻsmaydigan ekinlar paydo boʻlib, eman kamaygan, dehqonlar esa dala uchun oʻrmon kesgan: odamlar dehqonchilik boshlab, emanni kesgan. Sovuq aytilmagan, emanlar koʻpaymagan.
why.ru: Дико не растущие здесь культуры появляются, когда исчезают дубы, а земледельцы сводили лес под поля: люди начали пахать и рубить дубы. О холоде не сказано, и дубов стало меньше.

stem.en:
Two years ago, the village ______ a small museum of musical instruments in its old schoolhouse, and visitors now come from all over the region to see it.

why.en: "Two years ago" places the action in the past, so the simple past "opened" fits. "Opens", "will open" and "is opening" are present or future forms.
why.uz: «Two years ago» harakatni oʻtmishga joylaydi, shuning uchun oddiy oʻtgan zamon «opened» mos. «Opens», «will open» va «is opening» — hozirgi yoki kelasi zamon shakllari.
why.ru: «Two years ago» относит действие к прошлому, поэтому подходит простое прошедшее «opened». «Opens», «will open» и «is opening» — формы настоящего или будущего времени.

why.ru: Здесь встречаются два полных предложения, поэтому их соединяет точка с запятой. Одна запятая — ошибка, без знака предложения сливаются, а после «and» запятая не ставится.

The small guesthouse stands at the edge of a cliff above the sea. The sound of the waves breaking on the rocks below it ______ its guests to sleep every night.

why.uz: Ega — «The sound», birlikda, shuning uchun kesim «lulls». «Waves» va «rocks» tovushni tasvirlaydigan iboralar ichida; koʻplik shakllari egaga emas, ularga moslashgan.
